# `if` / `else`

```
if (condition) {
  ## code to run
}
```

```{r}
x <- 3
if (x < 4) {
  print(TRUE)
} else {
  print(FALSE)
}

# one-liner form
if (x < 4) print(TRUE) else print(FALSE)

# vectorized form: ifelse() works element-by-element on a whole vector
x <- c(3, 4, 6, 7, 0, 4)
ifelse(x < 4, TRUE, FALSE)
```

## Nested conditions: grading example

```{r}
set.seed(123)
marks <- round(rnorm(50, mean = 60, sd = 15), 2)
```

Categorize each mark: Fail [0-60), Pass [60-70), Good Pass [70-80),
Very Good Pass [80-85), Distinction [85+].

**Approach 1 — iterate over values directly:**
```{r}
category <- character(0)
for (m in marks) {
  if (m >= 0 & m < 60) {
    category <- c(category, "Fail")
  } else if (m >= 60 & m < 70) {
    category <- c(category, "Pass")
  } else if (m >= 70 & m < 80) {
    category <- c(category, "Good Pass")
  } else if (m >= 80 & m < 85) {
    category <- c(category, "Very Good Pass")
  } else {
    category <- c(category, "Distinction")
  }
}
head(df_marks <- data.frame(marks, category), 5)
```

**Approach 2 — iterate over indices:**
```{r}
category2 <- character()
for (i in seq_along(marks)) {
  if (marks[i] >= 0 & marks[i] < 60) {
    category2[i] <- "F"
  } else if (marks[i] >= 60 & marks[i] < 70) {
    category2[i] <- "P"
  } else if (marks[i] >= 70 & marks[i] < 80) {
    category2[i] <- "GP"
  } else if (marks[i] >= 80 & marks[i] < 85) {
    category2[i] <- "VGP"
  } else {
    category2[i] <- "D"
  }
}
df_marks$category2 <- category2
head(df_marks, 5)
```

**Approach 3 — vectorized with nested `ifelse()`:**
```{r}
category3 <- ifelse(marks < 60, "Fail",
              ifelse(marks < 70, "Pass",
               ifelse(marks < 80, "Good Pass",
                ifelse(marks < 85, "Very Good Pass", "Distinction"))))
all(df_marks$category == category3)
```

# `for` Loops

```{r}
m <- 10
for (i in 1:m) print(i)
```

```{r}
for (i in 1:10) {
  if (i %% 3 == 0) {
    cat(i, "is a multiple of 3\n")
  } else if (i %% 2 == 0) {
    cat(i, "is a multiple of 2\n")
  } else {
    cat(i, "is neither a multiple of 2 nor 3\n")
  }
}
```

## Exercise 1: odd or even

```{r}
for (i in 1:10) {
  if (i %% 2 == 0) {
    cat(i, "is even\n")
  } else {
    cat(i, "is odd\n")
  }
}
```

## Exercise 2: importing every CSV in a folder

Build the file path from parts using `paste()`/`paste0()`:
```{r}
paste("data", "csv", sep = "/")
paste0("data", "/", "csv")
```

List every CSV in a folder, then load them all into one list:
```{r}
dir.create("demo_csv", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(head(iris, 3), "demo_csv/iris_part.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(head(mtcars, 3), "demo_csv/mtcars_part.csv", row.names = FALSE)

file_names <- dir("demo_csv", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
file_names

data_list <- list()
for (f in file_names) {
  data_list[[basename(f)]] <- read.csv(f)
}
str(data_list)
unlink("demo_csv", recursive = TRUE) # clean up the demo files
```

# `while` Loops

```
while (condition) {
  ## code to run
  ## something that eventually makes condition FALSE
}
```

```{r}
i <- 0
while (i <= 10) {
  print(i * 2)
  i <- i + 10
}
```

## Exercise: dice streak game

Print "YOU WON!" the moment three 5s are rolled in a row.
```{r}
set.seed(42)
streak <- 0
rolls <- 0
repeat {
  rolls <- rolls + 1
  roll <- sample(1:6, 1)
  streak <- if (roll == 5) streak + 1 else 0
  if (streak == 3) {
    cat("YOU WON! (after", rolls, "rolls)\n")
    break
  }
}
```

## Exercise: interactive multiplication table

This one needs a live console, since `readline()` only works in an
interactive R session (not when a script is run non-interactively):
```{r eval=FALSE}
repeat {
  number <- as.numeric(readline(prompt = "Enter a number 0-9: "))
  cat(number, "x 2 table:\n")
  for (i in 1:10) cat(number, "x", i, "=", number * i, "\n")

  again <- readline(prompt = "Continue? (y/n): ")
  if (tolower(again) != "y") break
}
```

# `repeat`

```
i <- 0
repeat {
  ## code to run
  i <- i + 1
  if (something_happens) break
}
```

```{r}
i <- 0
repeat {
  print(i)
  i <- i + 1
  if (i > 5) break
}
```
